title.zh: 卷515 列傳三百二 土司傳四 贵州
title.en: Volume 515 Biographies 302: Native Chieftain Biographies 4: Guizhou
title.raw: 卷515 列傳三百二 土司傳四 贵州

sentences.zh: 貴州，古羅施鬼國，漢夜郎國，並牂牁、武陵郡地。

translations.literal: Guizhou was in antiquity the state of Luoshi Gui, the Han dynasty's Yelang state, and comprised the territory of the Zangge and Wuling commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou was anciently the realm of Luoshi Gui and, in Han times, the kingdom of Yelang, covering the lands of the Zangge and Wuling commanderies.

sentences.zh: 唐亦置播州、思州。

translations.literal: The Tang also established Bozhou and Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang, Bozhou and Sizhou were also established.

sentences.zh: 元置八番、順元諸軍民宣慰使司以羈縻之。

translations.literal: The Yuan established the various Military and Civilian Pacification Commissions of the Eight Fans and Shunyuan to keep them under loose control.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan set up the Eight Fans and Shunyuan pacification commissions to hold the region under loose imperial sway.

sentences.zh: 明靄翠、奢香最為效忠。

translations.literal: Under the Ming, Aicui and Shexiang were most loyal in service.
translations.idiomatic: In the Ming, Aicui and Shexiang proved the most steadfast in their loyalty to the throne.

sentences.zh: 後則播州之楊、永寧之奢、水西之安，為西南钜患，楊氏滅，為遵義、平越二府；

translations.literal: Later the Yang of Bozhou, the She of Yongning, and the An of Shuixi became great troubles of the southwest; when the Yang were destroyed, [the territory] became the two prefectures of Zunyi and Pingyue;
translations.idiomatic: Later the Yang of Bozhou, the She of Yongning, and the An of Shuixi grew into the gravest menace in the southwest; when the Yang were overthrown, their lands became the prefectures of Zunyi and Pingyue;

sentences.zh: 奢氏滅，為永寧縣。

translations.literal: When the She clan was destroyed, [it became] Yongning county.
translations.idiomatic: when the She were destroyed, their domain became Yongning county.

sentences.zh: 清初，黔省安氏猶強。

translations.literal: In the early Qing, the An clan of Qian province remained strong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qing, the An of Guizhou still held formidable power.

sentences.zh: 經孫可望之亂，未頒正朔，苗蠻蠢動，諸擅兵相攻者，蹂躪地方，無有寧日。

translations.literal: After the turmoil of Sun Kewang, the correct calendar was not yet promulgated, the Miao and barbarians stirred restlessly, and those who seized armies to attack one another trampled the region so that there was never a peaceful day.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Kewang's rebellion the new dynasty's calendar had not yet been imposed; Miao and tribal peoples stirred, and warlords who took up arms against one another ravaged the countryside until no day passed in peace.

sentences.zh: 順治十五年，經略洪承疇定貴州。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Shunzhi, Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou pacified Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 15 (1658), Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou brought Guizhou under control.

sentences.zh: 十七年四月，馬乃營土目龍吉兆等反。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the seventeenth year, the native official Long Jizhao of Manai camp and others rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Shunzhi 17 (1660), Long Jizhao, a tribal headman of Manai camp, and others rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 雲、貴既平，各土司俱奉貢賦，遵約束。

translations.literal: Once Yunnan and Guizhou were pacified, all the native chieftains presented tribute and taxes and obeyed regulations.
translations.idiomatic: After Yunnan and Guizhou were pacified, every native chieftain paid tribute and obeyed imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 龍吉兆收養亡命，私造軍器，奸民文元、胡世昌、況榮還等俱黨附之，遙結李定國為聲援，糾合鼠場營龍吉佐、樓下營龍吉祥歃血盟，掠廣西泗城州之土寨，安南衛之阿計、屯水橋、麻衣沖、下三阿、白屯等處，所過劫戮。

translations.literal: Long Jizhao harbored fugitives and secretly manufactured weapons; the wicked men Wen Yuan, Hu Shichang, Kuang Ronghuan, and others all joined his faction. From afar he allied with Li Dingguo as a supporting force, and together with Long Jizuo of Shuchang camp and Long Jixiang of Louxia camp he swore a blood oath, plundering the native stockades of Guangxi's Sicheng prefecture and the places Aji, Tunshuiqiao, Mayichong, Xiasan'a, and Baitun in Annan guard, looting everywhere they passed.
translations.idiomatic: Long Jizhao sheltered outlaws and forged arms in secret; ruffians such as Wen Yuan, Hu Shichang, and Kuang Ronghuan flocked to him. He sought distant support from Li Dingguo, and with Long Jizuo of Shuchang camp and Long Jixiang of Louxia camp he bound himself by blood oath, raiding native stockades in Guangxi's Sicheng and sites around Annan guard—including Aji, Tunshuiqiao, Mayichong, Xiasan'a, and Baitun—pillaging wherever they marched.

sentences.zh: 總督趙廷臣、巡撫卞三元招諭不服，乃合疏請討。

translations.literal: Governor-General Zhao Tingchen and Provincial Governor Bian Sanyuan summoned them to surrender but they refused; they then jointly memorialized requesting a punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Zhao Tingchen and Provincial Governor Bian Sanyuan offered terms of surrender, but the rebels refused; the two officials then jointly memorialized the throne for permission to attack.

sentences.zh: 十一月十九日，廷臣破果母寨，殺賊數千，擒吉兆子、吉佐妻，殲逆党文元、胡世昌於陣，遂乘勝破呷寨。

translations.literal: On the nineteenth day of the eleventh month, Tingchen stormed Guomu stockade, killed several thousand rebels, captured Jizhao's son and Jizuo's wife, and destroyed the traitors Wen Yuan and Hu Shichang in battle; then, pressing the victory, he took the Geba stockade.
translations.idiomatic: On the nineteenth of the eleventh month Tingchen stormed Guomu stockade, killing thousands of rebels and capturing Jizhao's son and Jizuo's wife; Wen Yuan and Hu Shichang fell in the fighting, and he pressed on to seize the Geba stockade.

sentences.zh: 吉兆閉寨拒守，官兵圍之。

translations.literal: Jizhao shut the stockade and held out; government troops besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhao barricaded himself in his stockade; imperial troops laid siege.

sentences.zh: 十八年二月，廷臣令官兵人持一炬，縱火焚其寨，破之。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighteenth year, Tingchen ordered each soldier to carry a torch and set fire to the stockade, breaking it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Shunzhi 18 (1661), Tingchen had every soldier carry a torch; they burned the stockade and took it by storm.

sentences.zh: 吉兆及逆党況榮還等皆伏誅，馬乃平。

translations.literal: Jizhao and the traitors Kuang Ronghuan and others were all executed, and Manai was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhao and his accomplices, including Kuang Ronghuan, were put to death, and Manai was pacified.

sentences.zh: 九月，劉鼎叛。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Liu Ding rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Liu Ding rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年正月，丹平土官莫之廉以隱匿劉鼎伏誅。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Kangxi, the Danping native official Mo Zhilian was executed for concealing Liu Ding.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Kangxi 2 (1663), Mo Zhilian, native magistrate of Danping, was executed for harboring Liu Ding.

sentences.zh: 金築土官王應兆與鼎通，總督楊茂勳討平之，鼎敗逃水西。

translations.literal: The Jinzhu native official Wang Yingzhao was in league with Ding; Governor-General Yang Maoxun suppressed them; Ding was defeated and fled to Shuixi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yingzhao, native magistrate of Jinzhu, had colluded with Ding; Governor-General Yang Maoxun crushed the revolt, and Ding fled in defeat to Shuixi.

sentences.zh: 七月，被獲伏誅。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, he was captured and executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was captured and put to death.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，逆賊常金印等謀反，伏誅。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, the rebel Chang Jinyin and others plotted rebellion and were executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Kangxi 3 (1664), the rebel Chang Jinyin and his confederates were executed for plotting revolt.

sentences.zh: 金印，上元人，自稱常遇春之後，從粵走黔，與水西安坤、皮熊等同謀反。

translations.literal: Jinyin was a native of Shangyuan; he claimed to be a descendant of Chang Yuchun, fled from Guangdong to Guizhou, and plotted rebellion together with An Kun of Shuixi, Pi Xiong, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyin, a man from Shangyuan, claimed descent from the Ming general Chang Yuchun; fleeing from Guangdong into Guizhou, he joined An Kun of Shuixi, Pi Xiong, and others in a conspiracy to rebel.

sentences.zh: 金印稱「蕩虜大將軍湘平伯」，偽造印敕旗纛，聚党陳鳳麟、高岑、起士英、米應貴等，煽誘諸土司為亂，為同黨陳大出首，俱就擒。

translations.literal: Jinyin styled himself "Grand General Who Sweeps Away the Barbarians, Earl Who Pacifies Xiang," forged seals, edicts, banners, and standards, gathered partisans Chen Fenglin, Gao Cen, Qi Shiying, Mi Yinggui, and others, and incited the native chieftains to revolt; his accomplice Chen Da informed on them, and all were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyin took the title "Grand General Who Sweeps Away the Barbarians, Earl Who Pacifies Xiang," forged imperial seals, edicts, and battle standards, and rallied followers including Chen Fenglin, Gao Cen, Qi Shiying, and Mi Yinggui to stir the native chieftains into revolt; his associate Chen Da turned informer, and the whole band was seized.

sentences.zh: 二月，水西宣慰司安坤叛。

translations.literal: In the second month, An Kun, Pacification Commissioner of Shuixi, rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month An Kun, pacification commissioner of Shuixi, rebelled.

sentences.zh: 初，經略洪承疇至沅，師不能進，承疇招安坤，許以如元阿盡、明靄翠故事，坤大喜，繳印歸誠，引大兵由小路進入貴陽。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou reached Yuan, the army could not advance; Chengchou recruited An Kun, promising him treatment like the Yuan's Ajin and the Ming's Aicui; Kun was greatly pleased, surrendered his seal and submitted, and guided the main force by a small path into Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou reached Yuan, his army had been unable to advance; Chengchou won over An Kun with promises modeled on how the Yuan had treated Ajin and the Ming had treated Aicui. Kun gladly surrendered his seal and led the main force along a hidden path into Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 滇、黔底定，敘坤功，許世襲，兼賜袍帽靴服采幣。

translations.literal: When Yunnan and Guizhou were settled, Kun's merit was recorded; hereditary succession was granted, together with robes, hats, boots, garments, silks, and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: After Yunnan and Guizhou were pacified, Kun was rewarded with a hereditary commission and gifts of robes, hats, boots, silks, and ceremonial goods.

sentences.zh: 朋總兵皮熊合謀，蠢蠢思動，蹤跡頗露。

translations.literal: He joined in conspiracy with Regional Commander Pi Xiong; they stirred restlessly and their tracks were quite exposed.
translations.idiomatic: He then conspired with Regional Commander Pi Xiong; their restless scheming soon left clear traces.

sentences.zh: 總督楊葆勳曰：「水西地方沃野千里，地廣兵強，在滇為咽喉，在蜀為門戶，若於黔則腹心之蠱毒也。

translations.literal: Governor-General Yang Baoxun said: "Shuixi has a thousand li of fertile land, broad territory and strong troops; for Yunnan it is the throat, for Sichuan the gateway—for Guizhou it is a poison in the very heart.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Yang Baoxun said: "Shuixi commands a thousand li of rich land and fields vast armies; it is the throat of Yunnan and the gateway of Sichuan, but for Guizhou it is poison lodged in the vitals.

sentences.zh: 失今不討，養癰必大。」

translations.literal: If we miss the chance to attack now, the abscess we nurture will surely grow great."
translations.idiomatic: If we fail to strike now, the ulcer we allow to fester will only grow worse."

sentences.zh: 乃請剿。

translations.literal: He then requested a punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized for a punitive expedition.

sentences.zh: 命總管吳三桂督雲、貴各鎮兵分東西兩路討之。

translations.literal: The order was given for Grand Coordinator Wu Sangui to supervise the garrison troops of Yunnan and Guizhou and attack in eastern and western columns.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui was ordered to command the Yunnan and Guizhou garrisons and advance against the rebels in two columns, east and west.

sentences.zh: 三月，三桂統十鎮兵由畢節七星關入，令總兵劉之復駐兵大方，遏其沖逸，分提督李本深統貴州四鎮兵由大方之六歸河會剿，屯糧於三岔河。

translations.literal: In the third month, Sangui led troops of ten garrisons in through Qixing Pass at Bijie, ordered Regional Commander Liu Zhifu to station at Dafang to block their breakout, and detached Provincial Commander Li Benshen to command the four Guizhou garrisons in a joint attack from Dafang's Liugui River, storing grain at Sanhe River.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Sangui led ten garrisons through Qixing Pass at Bijie, posted Regional Commander Liu Zhifu at Dafang to block any breakout, and sent Provincial Commander Li Benshen with the four Guizhou garrisons to join the assault from Liugui River near Dafang, stockpiling grain at Sanhe River.

sentences.zh: 而檄黔省兵書誤書「六歸」為「陸廣」，於是本深兵及黔、蜀二省所運之糧盡屯陸廣，三路氣息隔絕不相通。

translations.literal: But in the dispatch to Guizhou troops "Liugui" was mistakenly written as "Luguang," so Benshen's force and all grain transported by Guizhou and Sichuan were stockpiled at Luguang; the three routes were cut off from one another and could not communicate.
translations.idiomatic: A clerical error in the Guizhou dispatch turned "Liugui" into "Luguang," so Benshen's troops and all grain shipped from Guizhou and Sichuan piled up at Luguang instead; the three columns lost contact with one another entirely.

sentences.zh: 三桂受困兩月，食將絕，外援不至。

translations.literal: Sangui was besieged for two months; provisions were nearly exhausted and outside relief did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui was trapped for two months; his food ran low and no relief came.

sentences.zh: 永順總兵劉安邦戰死，受圍益迫。

translations.literal: Yongshun Regional Commander Liu Anbang died in battle, and the encirclement grew tighter.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Liu Anbang of Yongshun fell in battle, and the ring of siege drew tighter still.

sentences.zh: 適水西土目安如鼎遣人偵黔營虛實，為本深所獲，始知三桂被圍已久，乃使為引導，整兵入援。

translations.literal: Just then the Shuixi native headman An Ruding sent men to spy on the strength of the Guizhou camp; they were captured by Benshen, who thus learned that Sangui had long been besieged; he made them guides, reorganized his troops, and marched to relieve him.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment An Ruding, a Shuixi headman, sent scouts to probe the Guizhou camp; Benshen captured them, learned how long Sangui had been surrounded, used them as guides, and marched in relief.

sentences.zh: 副將白世彥手斬驍賊以徇於陣，賊遂敗走。

translations.literal: Vice Commander Bai Shiyan personally beheaded a fierce rebel and displayed it before the ranks; the rebels then fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commander Bai Shiyan personally slew a fierce rebel and displayed the head before the army; the enemy broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 總兵李如碧亦率精兵入重圍，運糧接濟，兵合為一，敗賊阿作峒，復敗之得初峒，九月又敗之紅崖峒。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Li Rubi also led elite troops into the heavy encirclement, transported grain to supply them, and the armies united; they defeated the rebels at Azuo gorge, again at Dechu gorge, and in the ninth month again at Hongya gorge.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Li Rubi drove elite troops through the siege line with supplies; the forces united, routed the rebels at Azuo gorge and again at Dechu gorge, and in the ninth month defeated them once more at Hongya gorge.

sentences.zh: 坤率其妻祿氏逃於木弄箐，復逃至烏蒙，烏蒙不納。

translations.literal: Kun fled with his wife, the Lu clan, to Mulong ravine, then fled again to Wumeng; Wumeng would not receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Kun fled with his wife of the Lu clan to Mulong ravine, then on to Wumeng, which refused him shelter.

sentences.zh: 坤遣漢把曾經賚印投降，不許，生擒坤於大方之杓箐，並擒皮熊、安重聖等。

translations.literal: Kun sent the Han officer Zeng Jing bearing his seal to surrender; this was not accepted; Kun was captured alive at Shaojing in Dafang, and Pi Xiong, An Zhongsheng, and others were also captured.
translations.idiomatic: Kun sent his Han lieutenant Zeng Jing with the official seal to offer surrender, but the offer was refused; Kun was taken alive at Shaojing in Dafang, along with Pi Xiong, An Zhongsheng, and others.

sentences.zh: 皮熊不食十五日而死，坤與重聖俱伏誅。

translations.literal: Pi Xiong died after fasting fifteen days; Kun and Zhongsheng were both executed.
translations.idiomatic: Pi Xiong starved himself to death after fifteen days without food; Kun and Zhongsheng were executed.

sentences.zh: 四年十二月，郎岱土司隴安籓反，命吳三桂發兵討之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year, the Langdai native chieftain Long Anfan rebelled; Wu Sangui was ordered to send troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Kangxi 4 (1665), Long Anfan, native chieftain of Langdai, rebelled; Wu Sangui was ordered to march against him.

sentences.zh: 籓乃安坤親黨。

translations.literal: Anfan was a close associate of An Kun.
translations.idiomatic: Anfan had been a close ally of An Kun.

sentences.zh: 坤滅後，招納坤餘孽隴勝等，及安重聖妻隴氏，殺安順府經歷袁績，攻破關嶺，直犯永寧。

translations.literal: After Kun's destruction, he gathered Kun's remnant followers Long Sheng and others, and An Zhongsheng's wife of the Long clan; he killed Yuan Ji, registrar of Anshun prefecture, stormed Guanling, and pressed straight against Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: After Kun's fall he rallied Kun's surviving followers, including Long Sheng, and An Zhongsheng's widow of the Long clan; he killed Yuan Ji, registrar of Anshun, stormed Guanling, and drove straight toward Yongning.

sentences.zh: 隴勝等亦攻犯大定、威寧，殺畢節經歷秦文。

translations.literal: Long Sheng and others also attacked Dading and Weining, killing Qin Wen, registrar of Bijie.
translations.idiomatic: Long Sheng and his band also raided Dading and Weining, killing Qin Wen, registrar of Bijie.

sentences.zh: 五年六月，隴安籓伏誅，郎岱平。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year, Long Anfan was executed and Langdai was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Kangxi 5 (1666) Long Anfan was executed and Langdai was pacified.

sentences.zh: 二十四年七月，黎平賊何新瑞反。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-fourth year, the Liping rebel He Xinrui rose.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Kangxi 24 (1685) the Liping rebel He Xinrui rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 新瑞本李姓，初在靖州為僧，後至平茶所犯罪，逃至新化，乃冒姓何，稱故明總督何騰蛟子，煽惑苗民作亂，黎平官兵擊敗之。

translations.literal: Xinrui was originally of the Li surname; he first became a monk in Jingzhou, later committed a crime at Pingcha station, fled to Xinhua, then assumed the surname He, claimed to be the son of the former Ming governor He Tengjiao, and incited the Miao to rebel; Liping government troops defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Xinrui was born a Li; he had first taken vows as a monk in Jingzhou, then committed a crime at Pingcha station and fled to Xinhua, where he took the surname He and claimed to be the son of the Ming loyalist He Tengjiao, stirring the Miao to revolt until Liping troops routed him.

sentences.zh: 二十五年二月，新瑞伏誅，徙土司韋有能等，以其地入永從縣。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twenty-fifth year, Xinrui was executed; the native chieftains Wei Youneng and others were relocated, and their lands were incorporated into Yongcong county.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Kangxi 25 (1686) Xinrui was executed; native chieftains including Wei Youneng were resettled, and their territory annexed to Yongcong county.

sentences.zh: 廣順州之長寨，寨據各苗之腹。

translations.literal: Changzhai of Guangshun prefecture occupied the heartland of the various Miao.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhai in Guangshun prefecture sat in the very heart of the Miao country.

sentences.zh: 前總督高其倬誘擒阿近，議設營汛，以控前後左右各寨。

translations.literal: The former governor-general Gao Qizhuo lured and captured Ajin, and proposed establishing garrison posts to control the stockades before, behind, left, and right.
translations.idiomatic: Former Governor-General Gao Qizhuo had lured and captured Ajin and proposed garrison posts to control the surrounding stockades on every side.

sentences.zh: 雍正四年夏，官兵焚其七寨，未獲首逆，副將劉業浚即退營宗角，且言三不可剿。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourth year of Yongzheng, government troops burned their seven stockades but did not capture the chief rebel; Vice Commander Liu Yeji immediately withdrew the camp to Zongjiao and argued three reasons why suppression was impossible.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Yongzheng 4 (1726) government troops burned seven stockades but failed to seize the ringleader; Vice Commander Liu Yeji withdrew to Zongjiao and argued that suppression was impossible for three reasons.

sentences.zh: 鄂爾泰駁以三不可不剿；

translations.literal: Ortai rebutted with three reasons why suppression could not be avoided;
translations.idiomatic: Ortai countered with three reasons why they had no choice but to suppress them;

sentences.zh: 令總兵石禮哈搜討，盡殲首從，勒繳軍器，建參將營，分扼險要，易服薙發，立保甲，稽田戶。

translations.literal: He ordered Regional Commander Shi Liha to search and attack, exterminate leaders and followers, compel surrender of weapons, establish a vice-commander's camp, garrison strategic passes, change dress and shave the head, institute the baojia system, and register field households.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Regional Commander Shi Liha to hunt them down, wipe out leaders and followers alike, confiscate weapons, build a vice-commander's garrison at key passes, impose Han dress and shaved heads, institute the baojia system, and register farming households.

sentences.zh: 於是乘威招服黔邊東西南三面廣順、定番、鎮甯生苗六百八十寨，鎮寧、永寧、永豐、安順生苗千三百九十八寨，地方千餘里，直抵粵界。

translations.literal: Thereupon, riding the momentum, they won over on the eastern, southern, and western borders of Qian six hundred and eighty stockades of raw Miao in Guangshun, Dingfan, and Zhenning, and one thousand three hundred and ninety-eight stockades in Zhenning, Yongning, Yongfeng, and Anshun, a territory of more than a thousand li reaching straight to the Guangdong border.
translations.idiomatic: Riding this victory, they brought over six hundred and eighty raw-Miao stockades on Qian's eastern, southern, and western marches in Guangshun, Dingfan, and Zhenning, and another 1,398 stockades in Zhenning, Yongning, Yongfeng, and Anshun—more than a thousand li of country reaching the Guangdong border.

sentences.zh: 鎮遠清水江者，沅水上游也，下通湖廣，上達黔、粵，而生苗據其上游，曰九股河，曰大小丹江，沿岸數百里，皆其巢窟。

translations.literal: The Qingshui River at Zhenyuan is the upper reach of the Yuan River; downstream it connects with Huguang, upstream it reaches Qian and Yue, while the raw Miao held its upper reaches—the Jiugu River and the Greater and Lesser Dan Rivers—for several hundred li along the banks, all their lairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Qingshui River at Zhenyuan is the upper Yuan: downstream it opens on Huguang, upstream on Guizhou and Guangdong, while raw Miao held its headwaters—the Jiugu River and the Greater and Lesser Dan—for hundreds of li along both banks, their strongholds throughout.

sentences.zh: 古州者，有裡有外。

translations.literal: Guzhou had an inner and an outer [district].
translations.idiomatic: Guzhou was divided into inner and outer districts.

sentences.zh: 裡古州距黎平府百八十里，即元置古州八萬洞軍民長官司所也。

translations.literal: Inner Guzhou was one hundred and eighty li from Liping prefecture; it was the seat established by the Yuan of the Guzhou Ba Wan Dong Military and Civilian Chief's Office.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Guzhou lay 180 li from Liping prefecture, on the site of the Yuan's Guzhou Ba Wan Dong chief's office.

sentences.zh: 地周八十餘里，戶四五千，口二萬餘。

translations.literal: The territory measured more than eighty li around, with four or five thousand households and more than twenty thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: It covered more than eighty li square, with four or five thousand households and over twenty thousand people.

sentences.zh: 都江、溶江界其左右，合為古州江。

translations.literal: The Dujiang and Rongjiang bounded it left and right, joining to form the Guzhou River.
translations.idiomatic: The Dujiang and Rongjiang flanked it on either side and merged into the Guzhou River.

sentences.zh: 由此東西南北各二三百里為外古州，約周千二三百里，戶數千，口十餘萬，可敵兩三州縣。

translations.literal: From this point two or three hundred li to east, south, west, and north was outer Guzhou, roughly twelve or thirteen hundred li in circumference, several thousand households and more than one hundred thousand persons, comparable to two or three prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Two or three hundred li in every direction beyond lay outer Guzhou, roughly 1,200–1,300 li around, with thousands of households and more than 100,000 people—comparable to two or three full prefectures.

sentences.zh: 環黔、粵萬山間，而諸葛營踞其中，倚山面川，尤據形勢。

translations.literal: Amid the myriad mountains between Qian and Yue, Zhuge camp sat in the center, leaning on mountains and facing rivers, especially commanding the terrain.
translations.idiomatic: Amid the mountains between Guizhou and Guangdong, Zhuge camp sat at the center, backed by hills and facing the rivers—a position of exceptional strategic strength.

sentences.zh: 張廣泗守黎平，輕騎深入周勘，倡議置鎮諸葛營，扼吭控制，而其外戶為都勻、八寨，內戶為丹江、清江。

translations.literal: Zhang Guangsi guarded Liping, rode light cavalry deep in reconnaissance, and proposed establishing a garrison at Zhuge camp to seize the throat and control [the region]; its outer gates were Duyun and Bazhai, its inner gates Danjiang and Qingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guangsi, defending Liping, reconnoitered deep country by light cavalry and proposed a garrison at Zhuge camp to hold the region by the throat; Duyun and Bazhai were its outer gates, Danjiang and Qingjiang its inner gates.

sentences.zh: 乃于六年夏，先創八寨以通運道，分兵進攻大小丹江，出奇設伏，盡焚負固之雞講五寨。

translations.literal: Then in the summer of the sixth year they first established Bazhai to open the supply route, divided troops to attack the Greater and Lesser Dan Rivers, used surprise and ambush, and burned all five stockades of Jijiang that held out stubbornly.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Yongzheng 6 (1728) they first secured Bazhai to open the supply route, then divided forces against the Greater and Lesser Dan Rivers, using ambushes to burn all five stubborn Jijiang stockades.

sentences.zh: 苗赴軍乞降，飲血刻木，埋石為誓。

translations.literal: The Miao came to the army to beg surrender, drinking blood and carving wood, burying stones as oath.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao came to the army to surrender, drinking blood, carving wooden tokens, and burying stones to seal their oath.

sentences.zh: 九年，乘勝沿九股河下抵清水江。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, pressing the victory, they descended along the Jiugu River to reach the Qingshui River.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 9 (1731), riding their momentum, they pushed down the Jiugu River to the Qingshui.

sentences.zh: 時九股苗為漢奸曾文登所煽，言改流升科，額將歲倍，且江深崖險，兵不能入。

translations.literal: At that time the Jiugu Miao were incited by the Han traitor Zeng Wendeng, who said that conversion to direct administration would double the land tax yearly, and moreover that the river was deep and the cliffs perilous so troops could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiugu Miao had been stirred up by the Han collaborator Zeng Wendeng, who warned that direct rule would double their land tax every year and boasted that deep rivers and sheer cliffs would keep troops out.

sentences.zh: 及官軍至，以農忙佯乞撫，廣泗亦佯許之，而潛舟宵濟，扼其援竄。

translations.literal: When government troops arrived, [the Miao] pretended to beg for pacification on grounds of the busy farming season; Guangsi also pretended to agree, but secretly crossed by boat at night and cut off their routes of aid and flight.
translations.idiomatic: When government troops arrived, the Miao feigned a plea for peace, citing the busy farming season; Guangsi pretended to accept while secretly ferrying boats across by night to cut off their escape and reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 蘇大有、張禹謨突搗其巢，又敗其夜劫營之賊，填壕拔橛，冒險深入，苗四山號泣，縛曾文登以獻。

translations.literal: Su Dayou and Zhang Yumo suddenly struck their lair, again defeated the rebels who raided the camp by night, filled ditches and pulled up stakes, braved danger and advanced deep; the Miao wailed on four mountains and bound Zeng Wendeng to present him.
translations.idiomatic: Su Dayou and Zhang Yumo stormed their stronghold, repulsed a night attack on the camp, filled ditches and tore up palisades, and pressed deep into dangerous country; Miao on every side wailed, and they bound Zeng Wendeng and brought him in.

sentences.zh: 於是清水江、丹江皆奏設重營，以控江路，令兵役雇苗船百餘，赴湖南市鹽布糧貨，往返不絕，民、夷大忭，估客雲集。

translations.literal: Thereupon heavy garrisons were memorialized for both Qingshui River and Dan River to control the river route; soldiers and laborers were ordered to hire more than a hundred Miao boats to go to Hunan to buy salt, cloth, grain, and goods; traffic was unceasing; Han and tribes were greatly pleased, and merchants gathered like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy garrisons were then established on the Qingshui and Dan to control the river trade; troops hired more than a hundred Miao boats to carry salt, cloth, and grain to and from Hunan until traffic never ceased; Han and tribes alike rejoiced, and merchants flocked in.

sentences.zh: 古州自昔奧樸，自清初吳三桂偽將馬寶兵由楚竄滇，取道古州，諸苗遮獲其大砲重甲火藥，由是日強，而上下江尤甚。

translations.literal: Guzhou had always been remote and simple; from the early Qing, when Wu Sangui's false general Ma Bao's troops fled from Chu into Dian by way of Guzhou, the various Miao intercepted and seized their great cannon, heavy armor, and gunpowder; from this they grew stronger day by day, especially on the upper and lower rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Guzhou had long been remote and untouched; early in the Qing, when Ma Bao, a general of Wu Sangui's rebel regime, marched from Huguang into Yunnan through Guzhou, local Miao ambushed his column and seized heavy cannon, armor, and gunpowder—after which they grew steadily stronger, especially along the upper and lower rivers.

sentences.zh: 上江為來牛、定旦，下江為溶峒。

translations.literal: The upper river was Lainiu and Dingdan; the lower river was Rongdong.
translations.idiomatic: The upper river country was Lainiu and Dingdan; the lower was Rongdong.

sentences.zh: 當廣泗初至，苗皆謂官兵不能久，依違從撫，及聞諸葛營建城堡，遂群起拒命。

translations.literal: When Guangsi first arrived, the Miao all said government troops could not stay long and wavered in accepting pacification; when they heard that Zhuge camp was building a fortress, they rose in groups to defy orders.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangsi first arrived, the Miao assumed government troops would not stay long and vacillated toward peace; when word spread that a fortress was rising at Zhuge camp, they rose in arms across the region.

sentences.zh: 八年秋，廣泗督官兵夜半集苗船為浮橋，攻其不備，進攻上江之來牛、定旦，擒斬四千，獲砲械無算。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the eighth year, Guangsi supervised government troops who at midnight gathered Miao boats as a pontoon bridge, attacked when they were unprepared, advanced against Lainiu and Dingdan on the upper river, captured and beheaded four thousand, and seized countless cannon and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Yongzheng 8 (1730) Guangsi had troops assemble Miao boats into a pontoon bridge at midnight, struck unprepared enemies, and advanced on Lainiu and Dingdan on the upper river, killing or capturing four thousand and seizing countless guns and arms.

sentences.zh: 其下江溶峒之深遠大箐，危峰障日，皆伐山通道，窮搜窟宅。

translations.literal: As for the deep and distant great ravines of Rongdong on the lower river, where perilous peaks blocked the sun, they cut paths through the mountains and searched out every lair to the end.
translations.idiomatic: In the deep ravines of Rongdong on the lower river, where sheer peaks blocked the sun, they cut roads through the hills and hunted down every hideout.

sentences.zh: 乃遍勘上下江，濬灘險，置斥堠，通餉運。

translations.literal: They then surveyed the upper and lower rivers throughout, dredged dangerous shoals, set outposts, and opened supply transport.
translations.idiomatic: They then surveyed both rivers end to end, cleared dangerous shoals, posted watch stations, and opened supply lines.

sentences.zh: 其都江、清水江之間，有丹江橫貫，惟隔陸路五十餘里，為之開通，於是楚、粵商艘直抵鎮城外，古州大定。

translations.literal: Between the Dujiang and Qingshui River, the Dan River ran across; only fifty-odd li of land route separated them; this was opened up, and then merchant vessels from Chu and Yue reached straight to outside Zhenyuan city, and Guzhou was greatly settled.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Dujiang and Qingshui the Dan River ran crosswise, separated by only fifty-odd li of land; once that gap was bridged, merchant vessels from Huguang and Guangdong sailed straight to Zhenyuan, and Guzhou was firmly pacified.

sentences.zh: 初，世宗以廣泗招撫古州，不煩兵力，由知府逾年擢至巡撫，遣侍讀春山、牧可登至軍察之，並頒犒師銀十萬兩。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Shizong [Yongzheng Emperor], because Guangsi had pacified Guzhou by persuasion without troubling military force, promoted him from prefect within a year to provincial governor, sent Academician Reader Chunshan and Mu Kedeng to the army to inspect, and also issued one hundred thousand taels of silver to reward the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Yongzheng Emperor, impressed that Guangsi had pacified Guzhou by persuasion without major fighting, promoted him from prefect to provincial governor within a year, sent Academician Reader Chunshan and Mu Kedeng to inspect the army, and granted 100,000 taels to reward the troops.

sentences.zh: 鄂爾泰約廣西巡撫金鉷赴貴陽會籌邊事，乃議黎平府設古州鎮，而都勻府之八寨、丹江，鎮遠府之清水江，設協營，增兵數千，為古州外衛；

translations.literal: Ortai arranged for Guangxi Provincial Governor Jin Hong to come to Guiyang to confer on border affairs; they then proposed establishing Guzhou garrison at Liping prefecture, and at Bazhai and Danjiang of Duyun prefecture and Qingshui River of Zhenyuan prefecture establishing coordinated camps, increasing troops by several thousand as outer guards of Guzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Ortai summoned Guangxi Governor Jin Hong to Guiyang to plan border defense; they proposed a Guzhou garrison at Liping, coordinated camps at Bazhai and Danjiang in Duyun and on the Qingshui in Zhenyuan, and several thousand additional troops as Guzhou's outer defenses;

sentences.zh: 後復改清江協為鎮，與古州分轄。

translations.literal: Later the Qingjiang coordinated camp was again changed to a garrison, sharing jurisdiction with Guzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Qingjiang coordinated camp was upgraded to a full garrison, sharing jurisdiction with Guzhou.

sentences.zh: 世宗嘉鄂爾泰之勞，錫封襄勤伯，世襲罔替。

translations.literal: The Shizong commended Ortai's labor and enfeoffed him as Baron Xiangqin, with perpetual hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongzheng Emperor rewarded Ortai's service by ennobling him as Baron Xiangqin with perpetual hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 九年冬，入為武英殿大學士，以高其倬代之，以元展成巡撫貴州。

translations.literal: In the winter of the ninth year he entered the capital as Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory; Gao Qizhuo replaced him, and Yuan Zhancheng became provincial governor of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Yongzheng 9 Ortai was recalled to the capital as Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory; Gao Qizhuo replaced him in the field, and Yuan Zhancheng became governor of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 十二年，哈元生進新辟苗疆圖志，以尹繼善督雲、貴，而復有黔苗之變。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Ha Yuansheng presented a gazetteer atlas of the newly opened Miao frontier; Yin Jishan supervised Yunnan and Guizhou, and again there was turmoil among the Qian Miao.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 12 (1734) Ha Yuansheng submitted a gazetteer of the newly opened Miao frontier; Yin Jishan took charge of Yunnan and Guizhou, and unrest among the Guizhou Miao broke out again.

sentences.zh: 初，苗疆辟地二三千里，幾當貴州全省之半，增營設汛，凡腹內郡縣防兵大半移戍新疆。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Miao frontier had opened two or three thousand li of territory, nearly half of all Guizhou province; garrisons and posts were increased, and most of the defensive troops of the interior prefectures and counties were largely shifted to garrison the new frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The newly opened Miao frontier covered two or three thousand li—nearly half of Guizhou—and as garrisons multiplied, most defensive troops from the interior prefectures were redeployed to the new borderlands.

sentences.zh: 又鄂爾泰用兵招撫，止及古州、清江，未及台拱之九股苗。

translations.literal: Moreover, Ortai's use of force and persuasion had reached only Guzhou and Qingjiang, not the Jiugu Miao of Taigong.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Ortai's campaigns of force and persuasion had reached only Guzhou and the Qingshui, not the Jiugu Miao of Taigong.

sentences.zh: 有司輒稱台拱原內屬，巡撫元展成易視苗疆，遽於十年設營駐兵。

translations.literal: The officials readily claimed that Taigong had originally been internally subordinate; Provincial Governor Yuan Zhancheng took the Miao frontier lightly and hastily in the tenth year established a camp and stationed troops.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials insisted Taigong had always been under imperial control; Governor Yuan Zhancheng underestimated the frontier and hastily posted a garrison there in Yongzheng 10 (1732).

sentences.zh: 時秋稼未穫，苗佯聽版築，而刈穫甫畢，即傳集上下九股數百寨，叛圍大營，並扼排略大關之險，以阻餉道。

translations.literal: At that time the autumn grain was not yet harvested; the Miao pretended to accept fortification work, but as soon as the harvest was finished they summoned several hundred stockades of the upper and lower Jiugu, rebelled, besieged the main camp, and also seized the perilous pass of Pailue Daguan to block the supply route.
translations.idiomatic: While the autumn grain was still in the fields, the Miao pretended to accept the building works; the moment harvest ended they rallied hundreds of stockades of the upper and lower Jiugu, rebelled, besieged the main camp, and seized the Pailue Daguan pass to cut the supply road.

sentences.zh: 營中樵汲皆斷，死守彌月，援至始解。

translations.literal: Fuel-gathering and water-drawing in the camp were all cut off; they held out desperately for a full month before relief arrived and the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Wood and water for the camp ran out; the garrison held out for a full month until relief arrived and broke the siege.

sentences.zh: 提督哈元生入覲回黔，十一年春，進軍台拱，攻賊於番招之蓮花隘，破之，設戍其上。

translations.literal: Provincial Commander Ha Yuansheng returned to Qian after an audience in the capital; in the spring of the eleventh year he advanced on Taigong, attacked the rebels at Lianhua Pass in Fanzhao, defeated them, and established a garrison there.
translations.idiomatic: After an audience in the capital, Provincial Commander Ha Yuansheng returned to Guizhou; in the spring of Yongzheng 11 (1733) he marched on Taigong, routed the rebels at Lianhua Pass in Fanzhao, and posted a garrison there.

sentences.zh: 十三年春，苗疆吏以徵糧不善，遠近各寨蜂起，遍傳大刻。

translations.literal: In the spring of the thirteenth year, Miao frontier officials mishandled grain collection; stockades near and far rose like bees, and great placards were spread everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Yongzheng 13 (1735) corrupt grain levies by frontier officials set stockades rising far and near, and rebel proclamations spread everywhere.

sentences.zh: 總兵韓勳破賊古州之王家嶺，賊復聚集清江、台拱間，番招屯復圍於賊。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Han Xun defeated the rebels at Wangjialing in Guzhou; the rebels gathered again between Qingjiang and Taigong, and Fanzhao camp was again besieged by rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Han Xun defeated rebels at Wangjialing in Guzhou, but they regrouped between the Qingshui and Taigong, and Fanzhao camp was besieged again.

sentences.zh: 巡撫元展成與哈元生不合，倉卒調兵五千，盡付副將宋朝相領之赴援，半途亦困於賊。

translations.literal: Provincial Governor Yuan Zhancheng was at odds with Ha Yuansheng; he hastily mobilized five thousand troops and gave them all to Vice Commander Song Chaoxiang to lead to the relief, but halfway they too were trapped by rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Yuan Zhancheng, at odds with Ha Yuansheng, hastily dispatched five thousand men under Vice Commander Song Chaoxiang to relieve the camp, but halfway they too were trapped by rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊探知內地防兵半戍苗疆，各城守備空虛，於是乘間大入，陷凱里，陷重安江驛，陷黃平州，陷岩門司，陷清平縣、餘慶縣，焚掠及鎮遠、思州。

translations.literal: The rebels learned that half the defensive troops of the interior were garrisoning the Miao frontier and that each city's defenses were empty; they then seized the opportunity for a great incursion, taking Kaili, Chong'an River station, Huangping prefecture, Yanmen office, Qingping county, and Yuqing county, burning and plundering as far as Zhenyuan and Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that half the interior garrisons had been moved to the Miao frontier and that the cities were poorly defended, the rebels poured in, seizing Kaili, Chong'an River post, Huangping, Yanmen, Qingping, and Yuqing, and raiding as far as Zhenyuan and Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 而鎮遠府治無城。

translations.literal: Moreover, the seat of Zhenyuan prefecture had no city wall.
translations.idiomatic: The seat of Zhenyuan prefecture had no walled city.

sentences.zh: 人心恟懼，台拱、清江各營汛亦多為賊誘陷。

translations.literal: Hearts were alarmed and fearful; the various camps and posts of Taigong and Qingjiang were also largely lured and fallen to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Panic spread; many garrisons at Taigong and on the Qingshui were lured or overrun by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 逆氛四起，省城戒嚴。

translations.literal: Rebellious atmosphere rose on four sides; the provincial capital declared martial alert.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion flared on every side, and the provincial capital went on alert.

sentences.zh: 四月，哈元生乃以親兵三百自出督師，扼清平之楊老驛。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Ha Yuansheng then personally led three hundred of his own troops out to command, seizing Yanglao post in Qingping.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Ha Yuansheng marched out in person with three hundred of his own troops and seized Yanglao post in Qingping.

sentences.zh: 六月，詔發滇、蜀、楚、粵六省兵會剿，特授哈元生揚威將軍，湖廣提督董芳副之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, an edict ordered troops of six provinces—Dian, Shu, Chu, and Yue—to join in suppression; Ha Yuansheng was specially appointed General Who Displays Might, with Huguang Provincial Commander Dong Fang as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month an edict mobilized troops from Yunnan, Sichuan, Huguang, and Guangdong for a joint campaign; Ha Yuansheng was named General Who Displays Might, with Huguang Commander Dong Fang as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 七月，又命刑部尚書張照為撫定苗疆大臣，副都御史德希壽副之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Minister of Justice Zhang Zhao was also ordered to be Grand Minister for Pacifying and Settling the Miao Frontier, with Vice Censor-in-Chief De Xishou as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Minister of Justice Zhang Zhao was appointed Grand Minister for Pacifying the Miao Frontier, with Vice Censor-in-Chief De Xishou as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 時尹繼善已遣雲南兵二千星夜赴援，湖、粵兵亦繼至。

translations.literal: At that time Yin Jishan had already dispatched two thousand Yunnan troops to rush to aid by forced marches day and night; troops from Hu and Yue also arrived in succession.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yin Jishan had already sent two thousand Yunnan troops marching day and night to relieve the siege, and Hunan and Guangdong forces were arriving in turn.

sentences.zh: 生苗見各路援兵漸集，各擄掠回巢，棄城弗守。

translations.literal: The raw Miao, seeing relief troops from the various routes gradually gathering, each plundered and returned to their lairs, abandoning the cities and refusing to hold them.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing relief columns converging from every direction, the raw Miao plundered what they could and withdrew to their strongholds, abandoning the towns they had taken.

sentences.zh: 元生進軍凱里，檄各鎮克復諸城，又合攻重安江賊，以開滇師之路。

translations.literal: Yuansheng advanced his army to Kaili, ordered the various garrisons to recover the cities, and jointly attacked the rebels at Chong'an River to open the road for the Yunnan army.
translations.idiomatic: Ha Yuansheng marched on Kaili, called on the garrison commanders to retake the lost towns, and combined forces to attack the rebels at Chong'an River and clear the route for Yunnan troops.

sentences.zh: 生苗既回巢穴，則糾眾攻圍新疆各營汛，於是台拱、清江、丹江、八寨諸營復同時告急。

translations.literal: Once the raw Miao had returned to their lairs, they then mustered crowds to attack and besiege the various camps and posts of the new frontier; thereupon the camps of Taigong, Qingjiang, Danjiang, and Bazhai again all reported urgent distress at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: After retreating to their lairs, the raw Miao rallied to besiege Qing garrisons across the new frontier, and Taigong, Qingjiang, Danjiang, and Bazhai all sent urgent calls for help at once.

sentences.zh: 時廣西兵八千已至古州，廣東兵餉亦晝夜溯流而上，湖廣兵先後集鎮遠界。

translations.literal: At that time eight thousand Guangxi troops had already reached Guzhou; Guangdong provisions also ascended the river day and night; Huguang troops gathered at the Zhenyuan border in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Eight thousand Guangxi soldiers had reached Guzhou; Guangdong supply convoys were moving upriver day and night; and Huguang forces were assembling in turn on the Zhenyuan frontier.

sentences.zh: 元生遣古州鎮韓勳攻毀首逆各巢，又分兵三路：一由槁貢以通台拱，一由八弓援柳羅以通清江，一走都勻援八寨；

translations.literal: Yuansheng dispatched Han Xun of Guzhou garrison to attack and destroy the lairs of the chief rebels, and also divided the army into three routes: one from Gaogong to open Taigong, one from Bagong to relieve Liuluo and open Qingjiang, one through Duyun to relieve Bazhai;
translations.idiomatic: Ha Yuansheng sent Han Xun of the Guzhou garrison to storm the rebel chiefs' strongholds and split his forces three ways: one column through Gaogong to reach Taigong, one through Bagong to relieve Liuluo and open the route to Qingjiang, and one through Duyun to support Bazhai;

sentences.zh: 而八寨協副將馮茂復誘殺降苗六百餘及頭目三十餘冒功，於是苗逃歸者，播告徒黨，詛盟益堅，多手刃妻女而後出抗官兵。

translations.literal: Moreover, Assistant Brigade Commander Feng Mao of Bazhai again lured and killed more than six hundred surrendering Miao and over thirty chieftains to claim false credit; thereupon the Miao who had fled and returned spread word among their fellows, the oath-curse alliance grew firmer, and many cut down their wives and daughters with their own hands before going out to resist the government troops.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Brigade Commander Feng Mao at Bazhai then treacherously slaughtered more than six hundred Miao who had surrendered and over thirty of their chiefs to claim false merit. Fugitives who made it back spread word among their comrades, the blood-oath hardened, and many killed their own wives and daughters before going out to fight the government troops.

sentences.zh: 陷青溪縣城，而清江之柳羅、都勻之丹江，自春夏被圍半載，糧盡援絕，九閱月圍始解。

translations.literal: [They] captured Qingxi county seat; meanwhile Liuluo of Qingjiang and Danjiang of Duyun had been besieged from spring and summer for half a year; provisions were exhausted and relief cut off; only after nine months did the siege begin to be lifted.
translations.idiomatic: They took Qingxi county town. Liuluo on the Qingshui and Danjiang in Duyun had been under siege since spring—half a year with food gone and no relief—before the encirclement was broken after nine months.

sentences.zh: 張照奉命赴苗疆，且令察其利害。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhao was ordered on mission to the Miao frontier, and also commanded to investigate its advantages and harms.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao was dispatched to the Miao frontier with orders to assess the situation on the ground.

sentences.zh: 照至沅州、鎮遠，則密奏改流非策，致書諸將，首倡棄地之議，且袒董芳，專主招撫，與哈元生齟齬。

translations.literal: When Zhao reached Yuanzhou and Zhenyuan, he secretly memorialized that conversion to direct administration was not a good policy, wrote to the generals, first advocated the proposal to abandon territory, moreover sided with Dong Fang, exclusively advocated pacification through enticement, and was at odds with Ha Yuansheng.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Yuanzhou and Zhenyuan, Zhang Zhao secretly memorialized that pushing ahead with direct administration was a mistake, wrote to the field commanders urging withdrawal from contested territory, openly favored Dong Fang, and pressed exclusively for pacification—putting him at odds with Ha Yuansheng.

sentences.zh: 楚、粵官兵皆隸芳麾下。

translations.literal: The Chu and Yue government troops and officers were all under Dong Fang's command.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan and Guangdong troops all fell under Dong Fang's command.

sentences.zh: 旋議分地分兵，施秉以上用滇、黔兵，隸元生；

translations.literal: Soon they deliberated on dividing territory and dividing troops: above Shibing, Yunnan and Guizhou troops were used, subordinate to Yuansheng;
translations.idiomatic: They soon agreed to partition both territory and forces: north of Shibing would be handled by Yunnan and Guizhou troops under Ha Yuansheng;

sentences.zh: 施秉以下用楚、粵兵，隸董芳。

translations.literal: Below Shibing, Chu and Yue troops were used, subordinate to Dong Fang.
translations.idiomatic: south of Shibing by Hunan and Guangdong troops under Dong Fang.

sentences.zh: 於是已進之兵，紛紜改調互換，而哈元生、董芳遂欲將村寨道路盡畫上下界，文移辨論，致大兵雲集數月，曠久無功，賊乘間復出焚掠，清平、黃平、施秉間紛紛告警。

translations.literal: Thereupon the troops already advanced were confusedly reassigned and exchanged; Ha Yuansheng and Dong Fang then wished to mark upper and lower boundaries for all villages, stockades, and roads; documents and dispatches argued back and forth, causing the great armies to gather like clouds for months, idle and long without achievement; the rebels seized the opportunity to emerge again in burning and plunder; between Qingping, Huangping, and Shibing alarms were raised one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Troops already in the field were shuffled and reassigned; Ha Yuansheng and Dong Fang began drawing boundary lines through villages and roads and arguing over jurisdiction by dispatch. Great armies sat idle for months with nothing to show for it; rebels slipped out again to burn and loot, and alarms sounded repeatedly across Qingping, Huangping, and Shibing.

sentences.zh: 當是時，中外畏事者，爭咎前此苗疆之不當辟，目前苗疆之不可守，全局幾大變。

translations.literal: At that time, those inside and outside the court who feared trouble all blamed that the Miao frontier should not have been opened earlier, that the present Miao frontier could not be held, and the overall situation nearly changed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: At court and in the provinces alike, those who feared the cost of war began insisting the frontier should never have been opened and could no longer be held—the whole campaign teetered on the brink of reversal.

sentences.zh: 八月，召張照、德希壽還。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Zhang Zhao and De Xishou were recalled.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Zhang Zhao and De Xishou were recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十月，授張廣泗七省經略，哈元生以下鹹受節制。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Zhang Guangsi was appointed commissioner-in-chief of seven provinces; Ha Yuansheng and those below were all placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Zhang Guangsi was made commissioner-in-chief over seven provinces; Ha Yuansheng and the other commanders were all placed under his authority.

sentences.zh: 旋逮張照、董芳、哈元生及元展成治罪。

translations.literal: Soon Zhang Zhao, Dong Fang, Ha Yuansheng, and Yuan Zhancheng were arrested for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao, Dong Fang, Ha Yuansheng, and Yuan Zhancheng were soon arrested and brought to trial.

sentences.zh: 廣泗奏言：「張照等所以無功者，由分戰兵守兵為二，而合生苗、熟苗為一也。

translations.literal: Guangsi memorialized: "The reason Zhang Zhao and the others achieved nothing was that they split combat troops and garrison troops into two, yet combined raw Miao and pacified Miao into one.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guangsi memorialized: "Zhang Zhao and the others failed because they divided combat troops from garrison troops while treating raw and pacified Miao as a single enemy.

sentences.zh: 兵本少而復分之使單，賊本眾而復驅之使合。

translations.literal: The troops were already few, yet they were further divided to make them isolated; the rebels were already numerous, yet they were driven to unite.
translations.idiomatic: Our forces were already too few, yet they were divided further; the rebels were already numerous, yet they were allowed to rally together.

sentences.zh: 且各路首逆，自古州敗退，咸聚於上下九股、清江、丹江、高坡諸處，皆以一大寨領數十百寨，雄長號召，聲勢犄角，我兵攻一方，則各方援應，彼眾我寡，故賊日張，兵日挫。

translations.literal: Moreover, the chief rebels of the various routes, having been defeated and withdrawn from Guzhou, all gathered at Upper and Lower Jiugu, Qingjiang, Danjiang, Gaopo, and other places; each led dozens or hundreds of stockades from one great stockade, dominating and calling out, their power and momentum forming pincers; when our troops attacked one side, all sides sent support; they were many, we were few—therefore the rebels grew daily stronger and the army daily more defeated.
translations.idiomatic: After their defeat at Guzhou the rebel chiefs regrouped at Upper and Lower Jiugu, along the Qingshui and Danjiang, and at Gaopo, each great stockade commanding dozens or hundreds of lesser ones. They supported one another in a pincer. Whenever we struck one sector, the others came to its aid. They outnumbered us, so the rebels grew bolder while our armies kept losing ground.

sentences.zh: 為今日計，若不直搗巢穴，殲渠魁，潰心腹，斷不能渙其黨羽，惟有暫撫熟苗，責令繳凶獻械，以分生苗之勢。

translations.literal: For today's plan, unless one strikes straight at the lairs, annihilates the ringleaders, and routs the core, one absolutely cannot dissolve their followers; the only course is temporarily to pacify the acculturated Miao, charge them to hand over the guilty and surrender weapons, in order to divide the power of the raw Miao.
translations.idiomatic: The only way forward is to strike the heart of the rebellion—destroy the ringleaders and shatter their inner circle—or we will never break their following. For now we should pacify the acculturated Miao, require them to surrender fugitives and weapons, and thus split the raw Miao's strength.

sentences.zh: 而大兵三路同搗生苗逆巢，使彼此不能相救，則我力專而彼力分，以整擊散，一舉可滅，而後再懲從逆各熟苗，以期一勞永逸。」

translations.literal: Then the great army in three routes together would strike the rebel lairs of the raw Miao, so they could not rescue one another; then our strength would be concentrated and theirs divided; with orderly forces striking scattered ones, they could be destroyed in one blow; afterward the various acculturated Miao who followed the rebellion would be punished, in hope of one labor and lasting ease."
translations.idiomatic: Then send the main force in three columns against the raw Miao strongholds so they cannot aid one another—our strength concentrated, theirs divided. Strike the scattered enemy with disciplined troops and we can wipe them out in one campaign; only then punish the acculturated Miao who joined the revolt, and secure a lasting peace."

sentences.zh: 廣泗乃調全黔兵集鎮遠，以通雲、貴往來大路。

translations.literal: Guangsi then mobilized all Guizhou troops to assemble at Zhenyuan, to open the great road of travel back and forth between Yun and Gui.
translations.idiomatic: With that plan in hand Zhang Guangsi mustered all Guizhou troops at Zhenyuan to secure the main route between Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 以精兵四千餘攻上九股，四千餘攻下九股，而自統五千餘攻清江下流各寨，是冬，刻期並舉。

translations.literal: With more than four thousand elite troops he attacked Upper Jiugu, more than four thousand attacked Lower Jiugu, and he himself commanded more than five thousand to attack the various stockades downstream on Qingjiang; that winter, on a fixed date, all moved together.
translations.idiomatic: He sent over four thousand seasoned troops against Upper Jiugu and as many against Lower Jiugu, while personally leading more than five thousand against stockades downstream on the Qingshui. That winter all three columns struck on a fixed schedule.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年春，復增兵分八路排剿抗拒逆寨，遺孽盡竄牛皮大箐。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Qianlong, more troops were added and divided into eight routes for progressive suppression of resisting rebel stockades; the surviving remnants all fled into Niupi Great Gorge.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Qianlong 1 (1736) he reinforced the army and sent eight columns to sweep rebel stockades one by one; the survivors all fled into the Niupi Great Gorge.

sentences.zh: 箐圜苗巢之中，盤亙數百里，北丹江，南古州，西都勻、八寨，東清江、台拱，危岩切雲，老樾蔽天，霧雨冥冥，蛇虺所國，雖近地苗蠻，亦無能悉其幽邃，故首逆諸苗咸藪伏其中，恃官兵所萬不能至，俟軍退復圖出沒。

translations.literal: The gorge lay amid Miao lairs, coiling for several hundred li; north Danjiang, south Guzhou, west Duyun and Bazhai, east Qingjiang and Taigong; perilous cliffs sliced the clouds, ancient shade trees blotted the sky, mist and rain were dim; it was the domain of serpents and vipers; even nearby Miao barbarians could not fully know its hidden depths; therefore the chief rebel Miao all lurked and hid within, relying on the impossibility of government troops reaching there, waiting for the army to withdraw to plan raids in and out.
translations.idiomatic: The gorge lay deep in Miao territory, winding for hundreds of li—bounded by the Danjiang on the north, Guzhou on the south, Duyun and Bazhai on the west, and the Qingshui and Taigong on the east. Cliffs rose to the clouds, ancient forest blocked out the sky, and mist and rain hung constant; serpents thrived there. Even local Miao knew only part of its hidden reaches. The rebel chiefs hid inside, counting on the army's inability to penetrate, and waited to raid again once the troops withdrew.

sentences.zh: 廣泗檄諸軍分扼箐口以坐困之，又旁布奇兵箐外以截逋逸，如阹獸網魚，重重合圍，以漸進偪。

translations.literal: Guangsi ordered the armies to hold separately the mouths of the gorge to wear them down by siege; also stationed surprise troops outside the gorge to cut off fugitives, like penning beasts and netting fish, layer upon layer closing the encirclement, advancing and pressing gradually.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guangsi ordered the armies to block every gorge mouth and starve the rebels out, while posting ambush forces outside to cut off escape—as if penning beasts or netting fish—in tightening rings that closed in step by step.

sentences.zh: 自四月至五月，將士犯瘴癘，冒榛莽，靡奧不搜，靡險不剔，並許其黨自相斬捕除罪。

translations.literal: From the fourth month to the fifth month, officers and soldiers braved malarial vapors, entered brambles and thickets, searched every hidden recess, cleared every perilous place, and also permitted their followers to kill and capture one another to expiate guilt.
translations.idiomatic: From the fourth to the fifth month soldiers endured malaria and pushed through thicket and scrub, searching every hollow and clearing every cliff. They even allowed rebels to kill or capture one another in exchange for pardon.

sentences.zh: 由是憝魁罔漏，俘馘萬計，其饑餓顛隕死崖谷間者，不可計數。

translations.literal: From this the hardened chiefs had none who escaped; captives and severed heads numbered in the tens of thousands; those who starved, fell, and died in cliff valleys were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Not one hardened chief escaped; prisoners and severed heads numbered in the tens of thousands, and countless more starved or fell to their deaths in the ravines.

sentences.zh: 六年，復乘兵威搜剿附逆熟苗，分首惡、次惡、脅從三等，涉秋徂暑，先後埽蕩，共毀除千有二百二十四寨，赦免三百八十有八寨，陣斬萬有七千六百有奇，俘二萬五千有奇，獲銃砲四萬六千五百有奇，刀矛弓弩標甲十有四萬八千有奇。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, again exploiting military might to search out and suppress acculturated Miao who followed the rebellion, dividing them into three grades—chief evil, secondary evil, and coerced followers—from autumn through summer, successively sweeping clean; in all 1,224 stockades were destroyed and removed, 388 stockades pardoned, 17,600-odd slain in battle, 25,000-odd taken captive, 46,500-odd firelocks and cannon captured, 148,000-odd spears, halberds, bows, crossbows, flags, and armor.
translations.idiomatic: Over the next six years he used the army's momentum to mop up acculturated Miao who had joined the revolt, sorting them into chief culprits, lesser offenders, and the coerced. Campaign followed campaign through seasons hot and cold until 1,224 stockades were destroyed, 388 pardoned, more than 17,600 rebels killed in battle, more than 25,000 taken prisoner, and more than 46,500 firearms and cannon captured along with over 148,000 blades, bows, crossbows, banners, and suits of armor.

sentences.zh: 宥其半俘，收其叛產，設九衛，屯田養兵戍之。

translations.literal: Half of the captives were pardoned; their rebel property was confiscated; nine guards were established; garrison farming was set up to feed and station troops to guard them.
translations.idiomatic: Half the prisoners were released; rebel lands were confiscated; nine military colonies were established and settled with garrison troops to hold the region.

sentences.zh: 詔盡豁新疆錢糧，永不徵收，以杜官胥之擾。

translations.literal: An edict fully exempted grain taxes of the new frontier, never to be levied again, to stop harassment by government clerks.
translations.idiomatic: An edict exempted the new frontier from grain levies forever, to keep corrupt officials from preying on the people.

sentences.zh: 其苗訟仍從苗俗處分，不拘律例。

translations.literal: Miao lawsuits still followed Miao custom in disposition, not bound by legal statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Miao legal disputes were still settled by Miao custom, not Qing statute.

sentences.zh: 以廣泗總督貴州兼管巡撫事，世襲輕車都尉。

translations.literal: Guangsi was made governor of Guizhou and also charged with the duties of provincial governor; hereditary Commandant of Light Chariots was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guangsi was made governor of Guizhou with the powers of provincial governor and granted the hereditary rank of Commandant of Light Chariots.

sentences.zh: 自是南夷遂不反。

translations.literal: From this the southern barbarians then did not rebel again.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the peoples of the south did not rise again.

sentences.zh: 五年夏，湖南靖州、武岡瑤，城步橫嶺苗，與廣西瑤同叛。

translations.literal: In the fifth year summer, the Yao of Jingzhou and Wugang in Hunan, the Hengling Miao of Chengbu, rebelled together with the Yao of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fifth year the Yao of Jingzhou and Wugang in Hunan and the Hengling Miao of Chengbu rose together with Guangxi's Yao.

sentences.zh: 總督班第使鎮筸總兵劉策名以兵五千進剿，以五千應援，詔廣泗復以欽差大臣節制軍務。

translations.literal: Governor-General Bandi sent Zhen'gan Commander Liu Ceming with five thousand troops to advance in suppression, five thousand as relief; an edict again made Guangsi Imperial Commissioner to command military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Bandi sent Zhen'gan Commander Liu Ceming with five thousand men to suppress the revolt and five thousand as reserves; Zhang Guangsi was again appointed Imperial Commissioner to direct the campaign.

sentences.zh: 先後斬馘五千餘，俘五千餘，於十二月班師。

translations.literal: In succession more than five thousand were beheaded or severed, more than five thousand captured; in the twelfth month the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: More than five thousand were killed and another five thousand captured before the army withdrew in the twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 鄂爾泰卒於乾隆十年，以開闢西南夷功，配享太廟。

translations.literal: Ortai died in the tenth year of Qianlong; for his merit in opening and pacifying the southwestern barbarians, he was granted posthumous sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Ortai died in Qianlong 10 (1745); for his role in opening the southwest he was granted posthumous worship in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 後乾隆六十年，松桃苗變；

translations.literal: Later, in the sixtieth year of Qianlong, the Songtao Miao rebelled;
translations.idiomatic: Later, in Qianlong 60 (1795), the Songtao Miao rose in revolt;

sentences.zh: 及咸豐二年，教匪變，煽及苗疆，同治十二年方定。

translations.literal: And in the second year of Xianfeng, the sect rebels rebelled, inciting to the Miao frontier; only in the twelfth year of Tongzhi was it settled.
translations.idiomatic: in Xianfeng 2 (1852) sectarian rebels stirred trouble that spread into the Miao country, which was not pacified until Tongzhi 12 (1873).

sentences.zh: 然非土司肇事，故不錄。

translations.literal: Yet because native chieftains did not initiate the trouble, it is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Those outbreaks were not led by native chieftains, so they are not recorded here.

sentences.zh: 中曹長官司，在府南十五里。

translations.literal: The Zhongcao Chief's Office was fifteen li south of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhongcao chief's office lay fifteen li south of the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 明洪武三年，以謝石寶為長官司。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu of the Ming, Xie Shibao was appointed Chief's Office.
translations.idiomatic: In Ming Hongwu 3 (1370), Xie Shibao was appointed chief of the office.

sentences.zh: 傳至謝正倫，清順治十五年，歸附，仍准世襲。

translations.literal: The line passed to Xie Zhenglun; in the fifteenth year of Shunzhi of the Qing, he submitted, and hereditary succession was still permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The line descended to Xie Zhenglun, who submitted in Qing Shunzhi 15 (1658) and was allowed to retain hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 副司，劉氏，清雍正七年，於土權疊害案內改流官。

translations.literal: Deputy office: the Liu clan; in the seventh year of Yongzheng of the Qing, within the case of Tu Quandie's murder, conversion to regular officials was enacted.
translations.idiomatic: The deputy office, held by the Liu clan, was converted to direct administration in Yongzheng 7 (1729) during the investigation into Tu Quandie's murder.

sentences.zh: 養龍長官司，在府北二百二十里。

translations.literal: The Yanglong Chief's Office was two hundred and twenty li north of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Yanglong chief's office lay two hundred and twenty li north of the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 明洪武五年，以蔡普為長官司。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Hongwu of the Ming, Cai Pu was appointed Chief's Office.
translations.idiomatic: In Ming Hongwu 5 (1372), Cai Pu was appointed chief of the office.

sentences.zh: 傳至蔡瑛，清康熙八年，歸附，准世襲。

translations.literal: The line passed to Cai Ying; in the eighth year of Kangxi of the Qing, he submitted, and hereditary succession was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The line descended to Cai Ying, who submitted in Qing Kangxi 8 (1669) and was granted hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 白納長官司，在府南七十里。

translations.literal: The Baina Chief's Office was seventy li south of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Baina chief's office lay seventy li south of the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 元為白納縣，尋改。

translations.literal: Under the Yuan it was Baina county; soon it was changed.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan it was Baina county before the designation was changed.

sentences.zh: 明初，以周可敬為長官司。

translations.literal: In the early Ming, Zhou Kejing was appointed Chief's Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Ming, Zhou Kejing was appointed chief of the office.

sentences.zh: 傳至周爾齡，清順治十五年，歸附，仍准世襲。

translations.literal: The line passed to Zhou Erling; in the fifteenth year of Shunzhi of the Qing, he submitted, and hereditary succession was still permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The line descended to Zhou Erling, who submitted in Qing Shunzhi 15 (1658) and was allowed to retain hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 副長官。

translations.literal: Deputy native official.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy native official.

sentences.zh: 趙啟賢同。

translations.literal: Zhao Qixian likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Qixian served likewise.

sentences.zh: 虎墜長官司，在府東六十里。

translations.literal: The Huzhui Chief's Office was sixty li east of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Huzhui chief's office lay sixty li east of the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 明洪武三年，以宋璢為長官司。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu of the Ming, Song Lin was appointed Chief's Office.
translations.idiomatic: In Ming Hongwu 3 (1370), Song Lin was appointed chief of the office.

sentences.zh: 傳至宋繼榮，清順治十六年，歸附，仍准世襲。

translations.literal: The line passed to Song Jirong; in the sixteenth year of Shunzhi of the Qing, he submitted, and hereditary succession was still permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The line descended to Song Jirong, who submitted in Qing Shunzhi 16 (1659) and was allowed to retain hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 程番長官司，唐末，程元龍平定溪洞，世守程番。

translations.literal: Cheng Fan Chief's Office: at the end of the Tang, Cheng Yuanlong pacified the stream grottoes and for generations guarded Cheng Fan.
translations.idiomatic: The Cheng Fan chief's office: at the end of the Tang, Cheng Yuanlong pacified the stream valleys and his line guarded Cheng Fan for generations.

sentences.zh: 元改給安撫司印。

translations.literal: Under the Yuan the seal of a Pacification Commission was reissued.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan the office was reissued the seal of a pacification commission.

translations.literal: Shuixi Pacification Commission: In the third year of Kangxi, Wu Sangui destroyed An Kun and reorganized [the territory] into four prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The Shuixi pacification commission: in Kangxi 3 (1664) Wu Sangui overthrew An Kun and established four prefectures in its place.

sentences.zh: 二十一年十二月，諭大學士曰：「吳三桂未叛時，征討水西，曾滅土司安坤，其妻祿氏奔於烏蒙，後生子安世宗。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the twenty-first year, [the Emperor] instructed the Grand Secretaries, saying: "Before Wu Sangui rebelled, in his campaign against Shuixi he once destroyed the native chieftain An Kun; An Kun's wife Lady Lu fled to Wumeng and later bore a son, An Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Kangxi 21 (1682) the Emperor told the Grand Secretaries: "Before Wu Sangui rebelled, in campaigning against Shuixi he had destroyed the native chieftain An Kun; An Kun's wife, Lady Lu, fled to Wumeng and later bore a son, An Shizong.

sentences.zh: 朕觀平越、黔西、威寧、大定四府原屬苗蠻，以土司專轄，方為至便。

translations.literal: I observe that the four prefectures of Pingyue, Qianxi, Weining, and Dading originally belonged to the Miao and barbarians; exclusive native-chieftain jurisdiction would be most convenient.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that Pingyue, Qianxi, Weining, and Dading originally lay in Miao country; exclusive rule by a native chieftain would be the most practical arrangement.

sentences.zh: 大兵進取雲南，祿氏曾前接濟，著有勤勞，仍復設宣慰使，令世宗承襲。」

translations.literal: When the imperial army advanced to take Yunnan, Lady Lu had gone forward to provide supplies and had rendered notable service; the pacification commissioner was therefore restored, and Shizong was ordered to succeed to the office."
translations.idiomatic: When the great army marched to recover Yunnan, Lady Lu had gone ahead to supply the troops and rendered notable service; the pacification commission was therefore restored and Shizong was permitted to inherit it."

sentences.zh: 四十年，總督王繼文以土司安世宗為吏民之害，仍請停襲，地方歸流官管轄。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year, Governor-General Wang Jiwen, on the ground that the native chieftain An Shizong was a harm to officials and the people, again requested suspension of succession, and that the region be placed under direct official administration.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 40 (1701), Governor-General Wang Jiwen, citing An Shizong's harm to officials and people, again requested that succession be halted and the territory placed under direct administration.
